new_entities.name: Topical caffeine
new_entities.description: Topically applied caffeine-containing shampoos or scalp formulations used with the aim of reducing hair loss or improving hair growth characteristics.

new_entities.name: Hair shaft thickness
new_entities.description: Measured hair diameter or shaft-thickness outcomes in people using topical hair-growth products.

edges.population: adults with pattern hair loss or self-reported hair thinning using caffeine-containing shampoos or scalp formulations
edges.mechanism: Caffeine may increase intracellular cAMP signaling and prolong anagen biology in follicles, but real-world topical studies usually combine it with other actives, making shaft-thickness effects difficult to isolate.
edges.summary: Topical caffeine is promising for hair-loss care, but the evidence for making individual hairs thicker is much shakier than the marketing. Trials show better density and less shedding more consistently than actual shaft-thickness gains, so a mixed call is the most honest one.
edges.caveats: Most positive studies use combination products that include adenosine or other actives. Even the newest systematic review concluded that topical caffeine is promising overall, but standardized thickness outcomes remain inconsistent.
